_description: Comprehensive grade-by-grade CCSS ELA strands (Reading Literature, Informational, Foundational Skills, Writing, Speaking & Listening, and Language).

ela.name: Language Arts
ela.desc: Foundational reading, writing, literature, comprehension, and language mechanics aligned to Common Core standards.

ccss.title: Pre-K Early Literacy & Language Foundations (CCSS Aligned)
ccss.overview: Foundational early literacy skills focusing on phonological awareness, alphabet recognition, print concepts, and expressive language skills to prepare children for Kindergarten reading success.
ccss.standards:
Reading: Foundational Skills (PK.RF)

PK.RF.1: Recognize that print carries meaning and demonstrate basic print concepts (book orientation, top-to-bottom, left-to-right progression).

PK.RF.2: Demonstrate phonological awareness: recognize and produce rhyming words, blend and segment onsets and rimes, and isolate initial sounds in spoken words.

PK.RF.3: Identify and name letters of the alphabet (focusing on common uppercase and lowercase letters) and recognize the sounds associated with their own name.

Speaking & Listening (PK.SL)

PK.SL.1: Participate in collaborative conversations with peers and adults in small and large groups; follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking).

PK.SL.2: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally by asking and answering questions about key details.

PK.SL.6: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly using complete sentences when appropriate.

Language & Vocabulary (PK.L)

PK.L.1: Demonstrate command of the conventions of spoken standard English grammar when speaking (use frequently occurring nouns and verbs, form regular plural nouns).

PK.L.5: Explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings (sort common objects into categories, demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring adjectives).
competencies: Alphabet recognition (names and sounds)
Rhyming and phonemic awareness
Print concepts & book handling
Active listening and expressive conversation
Categorizing words and concepts

ccss.title: Kindergarten English Language Arts (CCSS)
ccss.overview: Focus on mastering print concepts, phonological awareness, phonics, decoding simple words, reading emergent-reader literature, and expressing ideas through drawing, dictating, and early writing.
ccss.standards:
Reading Standards for Literature (RL.K)

RL.K.1: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

RL.K.2: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details.

RL.K.3: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.

RL.K.7: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear.

Reading Standards: Foundational Skills (RF.K)

RF.K.1: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print (follow words left to right, top to bottom; recognize that words are separated by spaces; recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters).

RF.K.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes): recognize/produce rhyming words; blend and segment syllables; isolate and pronounce initial, medial, and final sounds in CVC words.

RF.K.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills: demonstrate one-to-one letter-sound correspondences; associate long and short sounds with the 5 major vowels; read common high-frequency words (sight words) by sight.

RF.K.4: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.

Writing Standards (W.K)

W.K.1: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces (e.g., state a favorite book and reason why).

W.K.2: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts naming the topic and supplying facts.

W.K.3: Use drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or loosely linked events in order.

Language Standards (L.K)

L.K.1: Demonstrate command of conventions of standard English grammar: print many upper- and lowercase letters; use frequently occurring nouns, verbs, and prepositions.

L.K.2: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I; recognize and name end punctuation (periods, question marks, exclamation points); spell simple CVC words phonetically.
competencies: Letter recognition and sound correspondence
Phonemic segmentation and blending (CVC words)
High-frequency sight word recognition
Retelling stories with key details
Writing and illustrating simple ideas

ccss.title: 1st Grade English Language Arts (CCSS)
ccss.overview: Expanding reading fluency and accuracy, mastering digraphs and vowel patterns, identifying main ideas, recounting stories with moral lessons, and writing structured narrative, opinion, and explanatory texts.
ccss.standards:
Reading Standards for Literature (RL.1)

RL.1.1: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

RL.1.2: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.

RL.1.3: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.

Reading Standards: Foundational Skills (RF.1)

RF.1.2: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds: distinguish long from short vowel sounds; isolate and pronounce sounds in single-syllable spoken words.

RF.1.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics: know spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs (sh, ch, th, wh); decode regularly spelled one-syllable words (silent e, vowel teams); read words with inflectional endings (-ed, -ing); recognize grade-level irregularly spelled words.

RF.1.4: Read grade-level text with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

Writing Standards (W.1)

W.1.1: Write opinion pieces introducing the topic or book, stating an opinion, supplying a reason, and providing closure.

W.1.2: Write informative/explanatory texts naming a topic, supplying facts, and providing a sense of closure.

W.1.3: Write narratives recounting two or more sequenced events, including details, temporal transition words, and closure.

Language Standards (L.1)

L.1.1: Demonstrate command of grammar: use common, proper, and possessive nouns; subject-verb agreement; personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns; past, present, and future verb tenses.

L.1.2: Capitalize dates and names of people; use end punctuation for sentences; use commas in dates and items in a series; spell untaught words phonetically.
competencies: Decode single-syllable words and consonant digraphs
Distinguish long and short vowel sounds
Read aloud with accuracy, phrasing, and expression
Compose structured narrative and informative paragraphs
Punctuate and capitalize sentences accurately

ccss.title: 2nd Grade English Language Arts (CCSS)
ccss.overview: Deepening comprehension by asking and answering 5W questions (who, what, where, when, why), decoding multisyllabic words with prefixes/suffixes, expanding vocabulary, and writing multi-sentence structured compositions.
ccss.standards:
Reading Literature & Informational Text (RL.2 / RI.2)

RL.2.1 / RI.2.1: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

RL.2.2: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.

RL.2.3: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.

RI.2.2: Identify the main topic of a multi-paragraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.

Foundational Skills (RF.2)

RF.2.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics: distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words; decode two-syllable words with long vowels; decode words with common prefixes and suffixes; identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.

RF.2.4: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

Writing (W.2)

W.2.1: Write opinion pieces introducing the topic or book, stating an opinion, supplying reasons using linking words (e.g., because, and, also), and providing a concluding statement.

W.2.2: Write informative/explanatory texts introducing a topic, using facts and definitions to develop points, and providing a conclusion.

W.2.3: Write narratives recounting a well-elaborated event or short sequence of events with details, thoughts, and closure.

Language (L.2)

L.2.1: Use collective nouns, irregular plural nouns (feet, children, mice), reflexive pronouns (myself, ourselves), and irregular past-tense verbs (sat, hid, told).

L.2.2: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names; use commas in greetings and closings of letters; use apostrophes for contractions and frequently occurring possessives.
competencies: Decode two-syllable words with prefixes and suffixes
Answer 5W questions (who, what, where, when, why)
Determine central message or moral of stories
Write paragraphs with linking words and clear conclusions
Proper use of irregular verbs and punctuation

ccss.title: 3rd Grade English Language Arts (CCSS)
ccss.overview: Crucial transition from learning to read to reading to learn: citing text evidence explicitly, analyzing character motivations, identifying literal vs. non-literal language, and writing multi-paragraph essays.
ccss.standards:
Reading Literature & Informational Text (RL.3 / RI.3)

RL.3.1 / RI.3.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

RL.3.2: Recount stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details.

RL.3.3: Describe characters in a story (traits, motivations, feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.

RL.3.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language (e.g., idioms, metaphors).

RI.3.2: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.

Foundational Skills (RF.3)

RF.3.3: Know and apply grade-level phonics: identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes; decode words with Latin suffixes; decode multisyllable words.

RF.3.4: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression.

Writing Standards (W.3)

W.3.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and organizational structure.

W.3.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly using facts, definitions, and linking words.

W.3.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences using descriptive details and clear event sequences.

Language Standards (L.3)

L.3.1: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs; produce simple, compound, and complex sentences; ensure subject-verb and pronoun-antecedent agreement.

L.3.2: Capitalize appropriate words in titles; use commas in addresses and dialogue; form and use possessives; consult reference materials (dictionaries, glossaries).
competencies: Cite textual evidence directly for comprehension
Determine main idea and supporting details
Analyze character motivations and plot cause/effect
Distinguish literal from nonliteral language
Organize multi-paragraph opinion and explanatory writing

ccss.title: 4th Grade English Language Arts (CCSS)
ccss.overview: Deep textual analysis, making inferences, comparing multiple viewpoints, conducting research projects, analyzing figurative language, and mastering sentence variety and conventions.
ccss.standards:
Reading Literature & Informational Text (RL.4 / RI.4)

RL.4.1 / RI.4.1: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

RL.4.2: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.

RL.4.3: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., character thoughts, words, or actions).

RI.4.5: Describe the overall structure (chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text.

RI.4.8: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.

Foundational Skills & Fluency (RF.4)

RF.4.3: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (roots and affixes) to read unfamiliar multisyllabic words accurately.

RF.4.4: Read grade-level text with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression to support comprehension.

Writing Standards (W.4)

W.4.1: Write opinion pieces supporting a point of view with reasons and information, using clear organizational structure and transition words.

W.4.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly with illustrations, formatting, and precise vocabulary.

W.4.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

Language Standards (L.4)

L.4.1: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why); form and use progressive verb tenses; use modal auxiliaries (can, may, must).

L.4.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language (similes, metaphors), word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
competencies: Cite textual evidence to draw inferences
Determine theme and summarize literary texts
Analyze organizational text structures (cause/effect, problem/solution)
Conduct focused research projects using multiple sources
Master relative pronouns, adverbs, and progressive verb tenses

ccss.title: 5th Grade English Language Arts (CCSS)
ccss.overview: Synthesizing information across multiple texts, quoting accurately to defend analytical arguments, evaluating author arguments, and writing evidence-grounded research papers.
ccss.standards:
Reading Literature & Informational Text (RL.5 / RI.5)

RL.5.1 / RI.5.1: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

RL.5.2: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters reflect on challenges; summarize the text.

RL.5.3: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details.

RI.5.6: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent.

RI.5.9: Integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

Writing Standards (W.5)

W.5.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with logically grouped ideas and facts.

W.5.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas through grouping related information, headings, illustrations, and domain-specific vocabulary.

W.5.8: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work.

Language Standards (L.5)

L.5.1: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and their function in particular sentences; form and use the perfect verb tenses (have walked, had walked).

L.5.2: Use punctuation to separate items in a series; use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence; use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.

L.5.5: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context; recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.
competencies: Quote text accurately to justify conclusions
Integrate and synthesize information from multiple texts
Analyze how narrator point of view influences text
Write cohesive, multi-paragraph essays with domain vocabulary
Master perfect verb tenses and complex sentence punctuation

ccss.title: 6th Grade English Language Arts (CCSS)
ccss.overview: Rigorous textual analysis, evaluating the credibility and relevance of arguments, analyzing narrative structure and plot development, and composing formal argumentative and explanatory essays.
ccss.standards:
Reading Literature & Informational Text (RL.6 / RI.6)

RL.6.1 / RI.6.1: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

RL.6.2: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

RL.6.3: Describe how a particular story's or drama's plot unfolds in a series of episodes as well as how the characters respond or change as the plot moves toward a resolution.

RI.6.8: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

Writing Standards (W.6)

W.6.1: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence; introduce claims, organize reasons logically, use words/phrases to clarify relationships, and maintain a formal style.

W.6.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

W.6.7: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.

Speaking & Listening (SL.6)

SL.6.1: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

SL.6.3: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

Language Standards (L.6)

L.6.1: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive); use intensive pronouns (myself, ourselves); recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

L.6.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases choosing flexibly from a range of strategies (context clues, Greek/Latin affixes and roots).
competencies: Cite textual evidence for analytical assertions
Evaluate arguments and detect unsupported claims
Analyze plot progression, climax, and character changes
Draft formal argumentative essays with credible evidence
Grammar: pronoun case, intensive pronouns, and Greek/Latin roots

ccss.title: 7th Grade English Language Arts (CCSS)
ccss.overview: Advanced literary and rhetorical analysis: citing multiple pieces of evidence, identifying conflicting viewpoints, analyzing how authors construct arguments, and crafting nuanced argumentative compositions.
ccss.standards:
Reading Literature & Informational Text (RL.7 / RI.7)

RL.7.1 / RI.7.1: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

RL.7.2: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary.

RL.7.3: Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact (e.g., how setting shapes the characters or plot).

RI.7.8: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.

RI.7.9: Analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or advancing different interpretations of facts.

Writing Standards (W.7)

W.7.1: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence; acknowledge alternate or opposing claims; organize reasons logically; establish and maintain a formal style.

W.7.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

W.7.7: Conduct research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions for further research and investigation.

Language Standards (L.7)

L.7.1: Demonstrate command of grammar: explain the function of phrases and clauses; choose among simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal differing relationships among ideas.

L.7.2: Use a comma to separate coordinate adjectives (e.g., It was a fascinating, enjoyable book).

L.7.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings (allusions, connotations).
competencies: Cite multiple sources of textual evidence
Evaluate arguments for sound reasoning and sufficient evidence
Address and refute opposing viewpoints (counterclaims)
Analyze author perspective and bias across texts
Master complex and compound-complex sentence structure

ccss.title: 8th Grade English Language Arts (CCSS)
ccss.overview: Deep rhetorical evaluation, citing the strongest evidence to support complex analyses, analyzing how dialogue develops theme and character, and writing sustained research and argumentative essays.
ccss.standards:
Reading Literature & Informational Text (RL.8 / RI.8)

RL.8.1 / RI.8.1: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

RL.8.2: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to characters, setting, and plot.

RL.8.3: Analyze how particular lines of dialogue or incidents in a story or drama propel the action, reveal aspects of a character, or provoke a decision.

RI.8.6: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author acknowledges and responds to conflicting evidence or viewpoints.

RI.8.8: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

Writing Standards (W.8)

W.8.1: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence; introduce claims, acknowledge and distinguish claims from alternate claims; organize reasons logically; provide concluding section.

W.8.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas through well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information.

W.8.8: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and quote or paraphrase data avoiding plagiarism and following a standard citation format.

Language Standards (L.8)

L.8.1: Demonstrate command of grammar: explain the function of verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives); form and use verbs in the active and passive voice; form and use verbs in the indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional, and subjunctive mood.

L.8.2: Use punctuation (comma, ellipsis, dash) to indicate a pause or break; use an ellipsis to indicate an omission.

L.8.5: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., verbal irony, puns) in context.
competencies: Cite the strongest textual evidence for complex claims
Evaluate arguments, detecting logical fallacies and irrelevant evidence
Analyze the rhetorical impact of dialogue and dramatic irony
Synthesize research with formal citations (avoiding plagiarism)
Master verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives) and verb moods

ccss.title: High School English Language Arts (CCSS Grades 9-12)
ccss.overview: College and career readiness: critical analysis of seminal literary works and foundational historical documents, sophisticated rhetorical critique, independent multi-source research, and rigorous synthesis writing.
ccss.standards:
Reading: Literature (RL.9-12)

RL.9-12.1: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

RL.9-12.2: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account.

RL.9-12.3: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., complex characterization, multiple plotlines, nonlinear timeline).

RL.9-12.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone.

Reading: Informational Text (RI.9-12)

RI.9-12.6: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness, or beauty of the text.

RI.9-12.8: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning (e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court majority opinions and dissents).

RI.9-12.9: Analyze foundational U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (e.g., The Declaration of Independence, The Preamble, Lincoln's Second Inaugural) for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.

Writing Standards (W.9-12)

W.9-12.1: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence; introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish significance, distinguish from counterclaim(s), and develop claims thoroughly.

W.9-12.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

W.9-12.7: Conduct sustained research projects to answer a question or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry; synthesize multiple sources on the subject.

Language & Rhetoric (L.9-12)

L.9-12.1: Apply the understanding that usage is a matter of convention, can change over time, and is sometimes contested; resolve issues of complex or contested usage consulting references.

L.9-12.3: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

L.9-12.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings (hyperbole, paradox, subtle connotations).
competencies: Analyze multifaceted literary works and complex characterization
Evaluate foundational historical documents and legal reasoning
Detect rhetorical strategies, fallacies, and author bias
Write sustained research and persuasive thesis-driven essays
Master advanced stylistic conventions, rhetoric, and syntax
